title: Spare Parts Catalogue Matching from Photos
summary: Identify spare parts from customer or mechanic photos by reading part numbers, matching catalogue images and filtering by vehicle fitment, then confirm stock and price before quoting.

seo.title: Spare Parts Matching from Photos with AI | VipraTech
seo.description: AI that identifies spare parts from photos using part number OCR, catalogue image matching and VIN-based fitment, then checks stock and price.

problem.intro: Mechanics and customers send parts counters a photo of a worn brake pad, filter, lamp or sensor along with the car model and year. Finding the right part number means searching the electronic parts catalogue by model, variant and fitment, and the answer often depends on one experienced counter executive.

pain_points.title: Wrong parts and returns
pain_points.detail: Lookalike parts across variants, fuel types and model years lead to wrong orders, returns and an unhappy garage.

pain_points.title: Worn or missing part numbers
pain_points.detail: Stamped numbers wear off and labels peel away, leaving only the shape and a few markings to go on.

pain_points.title: Expertise concentrated in a few people
pain_points.detail: Fast, accurate identification depends on senior counter staff, which caps how many enquiries a counter can handle.

pain_points.title: WhatsApp enquiries pile up
pain_points.detail: Photo enquiries arrive all day and wait until someone has time to search the catalogue.

solution.overview: We build a parts identification service that takes a photo and vehicle details from WhatsApp or the counter app. It first narrows the search to the vehicle's fitment list, decoded from the VIN or RC details. It then reads any stamped numbers, labels or barcodes and compares the part's shape against catalogue images within that list, producing a ranked shortlist with the evidence for each candidate. Supersession and interchange tables are applied, and stock, price and alternate locations come from your DMS or ERP. A parts executive confirms the part number before a quote goes back on WhatsApp or an order is created.
capabilities: Reads stamped and printed part numbers, OEM labels and barcodes from photos
Narrows candidates by make, model, variant, fuel type and year from the VIN or RC
Compares part shape with catalogue images within the vehicle's fitment list
Applies supersession and interchange tables to reach current part numbers
Shows stock, price and alternate branch availability from the DMS or ERP
Handles intake and replies on WhatsApp with the confirmed part and quote

workflow.title: Receive the enquiry
workflow.detail: A photo and vehicle details arrive on WhatsApp or are captured at the counter.

workflow.title: Decode fitment
workflow.detail: The VIN or RC details are decoded to the exact model, variant and year to narrow the catalogue.

workflow.title: Read and match
workflow.detail: Part numbers and labels are read, and the shape is matched against catalogue images in the fitment list.

workflow.title: Confirm the part
workflow.detail: The parts executive confirms a clear leading candidate in one tap, or chooses from the shortlist when candidates are close.

workflow.title: Check stock and price
workflow.detail: Supersessions are applied, and stock and price are pulled from the DMS or ERP.

workflow.title: Quote and order
workflow.detail: The quote goes back on WhatsApp, and confirmed orders become a pick list or sales order.

inputs: Part photos from customers, mechanics or counter staff
VIN, RC details or model, variant and year
Electronic parts catalogue data and images under your licence
Stock and price from the DMS or ERP
outputs: Ranked candidate part numbers with fitment evidence
Confirmed part number and current supersession
Log of unmatched enquiries showing catalogue gaps
human_in_the_loop: The parts executive confirms every part number before a quote is sent. Safety-critical parts such as brake, steering and suspension components are always checked against catalogue fitment by staff.
integrations: Dealer management system or ERP such as Tally or SAP Business One
OEM electronic parts catalogue or licensed aftermarket catalogue data
E-commerce storefront or B2B ordering portal
guardrails: Matches only within the vehicle's fitment list unless staff widen the search
Shortlists instead of a single answer when candidates are close
Catalogue data used only under your licence terms
Every quote logged with the evidence used to identify the part
compliance_notes: Customer phone numbers and chat history handled under the DPDP Act 2023, with WhatsApp messages sent only to opted-in contacts.

pilot.scope: One dealer parts counter for one brand, covering fast-moving categories such as filters, brake pads, lamps and clutch parts.
deliverables: Catalogue and image index for the pilot brand
Plan for further brands and categories

what_we_measure.how: Whether the confirmed part number appears first or within the shortlist, checked against the executive's final choice.
Time from photo received to quote sent, compared with the current counter.
Returns logged as wrong part during the pilot.
Enquiries the system could not narrow down, grouped by category.

faqs.q: Does it work for multi-brand aftermarket parts?
faqs.a: Yes, if you have licensed catalogue data and images for those brands. Aftermarket identification leans more on fitment filtering and cross-reference tables, which we load during setup.

faqs.q: Where does the catalogue data come from?
faqs.a: From the OEM electronic parts catalogue your dealership already licenses, or from an aftermarket catalogue provider. We work within those licence terms and do not scrape catalogues.

faqs.q: What if the part has no visible number?
faqs.a: The system relies on vehicle fitment and shape matching, and shows a shortlist with catalogue images side by side. The executive can ask the customer for one more photo from a specific angle.

faqs.q: Can it handle two-wheeler and commercial vehicle parts?
faqs.a: Yes, provided catalogue data is available. Two-wheeler parts are often small and similar, so we pay particular attention to fitment filtering in those categories.
